newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone president pardons jailed army officer.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone president pardons jailed army officer.

text.p: Sierra Leone's president, Ahmad Tejan Kabbah, has pardoned a senior military officer jailed for life for treason in 1995 on charges of helping rebels.
Tejan Kabbah announced the pardon of Lieutenant Colonel Chernor Malado Deen, whose release had been repeatedly requested by the rebels, to mark the end of the Moslem fasting month of Ramadan.
Chernor, who commanded troops in the north of the country at the time of his arrest, is the highest-ranking officer convicted of treason by aiding the rebels, who took up arms in 1991.
Sierra Leone's government and the rebels agreed a peace deal in Ivory Coast in December but are still finalising implementation details. A ceasefire is in force.
Tejan Kabbah took office in March 1996 after multi-party elections ended four years of army rule.
